the combined rate is two apples per day.","reason":"The first constructs the wrong comparison ratio; the second omits a consumer when forming the total consumption rate.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02102","case1_error":"Leading answer marker says 20, but the derivation correctly calculates and rounds the serving time to 15 minutes.","case2_error":"Divides by servings per batch twice, treating the correctly calculated 15 batches as 15 servings and reducing production again.","reason":"The first has only an answer-marker conflict, so a shared or differing mathematical error mechanism cannot be established.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J02103","case1_error":"Provides correct total and division formulas, then gives unsupported 6186 instead of 859 without showing a numerical evaluation.","case2_error":"Reports the older brother's 11 cars as the three-person total, omitting Tommy's and Jessie's six cars from that total.","reason":"The first supplies an unsupported final number after correct formulas; the second answers with a component quantity instead of the requested total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02104","case1_error":"Omits Ted's four eaten cookies, reporting the amount remaining before his consumption.","case2_error":"Subtracts one bun per excluded guest instead of three, mixing guest counts with burger counts and obtaining 28 instead of 24 buns.","reason":"The first entirely omits a stated consumption event;
